summary_1line: In exile, Draupadi laments the Pandavas’ fall from royal luxury and urges Yudhishthira to feel anger and act against the injustice of the Kauravas.

image_candidates.scene_text: Draupadi in the forest, dressed in simple garments, passionately reproaches Yudhishthira seated on kusa grass while the Pandava brothers listen in silence.
Yudhishthira sits in worn deer-skin upon a bed of grass in the twilight forest, contrasting with Draupadi’s memory of his former jeweled ivory throne.
The mighty Bhima and Arjuna, once surrounded by royal splendor, now stand armed but austere among forest trees as Draupadi points to their undeserved hardship.
